Subject: POC traffic scope + acceptance checkpoints for Newton Analytics

Hi Sofia / Marcus — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed intake for the POC traffic profile and acceptance criteria.

Key hypotheses from today's discovery:
- Primary inference workload = real-time user-facing Recommendations API (100ms median latency target).
- Typical prompt sizes: 80–220 tokens at input, ~60–150 tokens generated per response.
- Expected baseline: 120 RPS steady-state for the first slice; 300 RPS peak burst windows (3–5 minutes) during marketing events.
- Concurrent user connections: ~250 concurrent client sessions across regions (US primary).

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will validate):
1) Latency under steady-state (120 RPS) and under 300 RPS burst with 250 concurrent sessions. Target: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms.
2) Token-cost estimate and runbook for autoscale + burst handling.
3) Correctness smoke-checks: sample 200 prompt/response pairs for functional parity with your current service.
4) Fault & fallback exercise: force a model variant fallback and validate graceful degradation.

Deliverables & timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange MOP (workload matrix) and sample prompts — I attached a starter MOP.
- Week 1: Redwood runs baseline perf on synthetic replay of your traffic (karthik + infra).
- Week 2: Live trial ingress with real traffic slice in our hosted sandbox (Ben to spin environment).
- Week 3: Evaluation readout, cost projection, and a short runbook with SLA options.

Owners / points of contact:
- Newton side: Sofia (POC owner), Marcus (infra lead).
- Redwood side: Lauren (AM / POC lead), Ben Carter (ops lead), Karthik Iyer (benchmarks + kernel tuning).

Acceptance criteria (suggested):
- Functional: 95% of sampled responses match expected intents/formatting (hand-off list of checks).
- Performance: p95 latency under acceptance window for steady-state and no unacceptable errors during burst tests.
- Cost: Estimated token/unit cost within 25% of your current spend baseline or clear tradeoffs documented.

Next steps:
1) Sofia: confirm the sample prompt set and whether we should include expanded cold-start prompts (yes/no) by Tue 11/3.
2) Marcus: confirm access pattern for replay and any IP whitelisting needed.
3) Redwood (Ben/Karthik): provision sandbox and post baseline numbers by 11/8.

Attachments: newton_poc_mop_v1.xlsx (workload matrix); Redwood SLA draft for POC.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min check-in after the baseline run.

Subject: Internal: sandbox capacity + fallback plan

Quick internal note (keeping in thread to preserve context):
- Sandbox: we can allocate a 2-GPU sandbox (A100-equivalent) in our hosted sandbox for Newton. That maps to ~350 RPS for the recommended quantized model under optimistic latency targets.
- Fallback policy options:
  a) Model-size fallback: switch to a 7B-ish variant during >250 RPS sustained for >90s. Pros: lower token cost. Cons: potential drop in recommendation relevance.
  b) Response-throttling: gracefully queue requests for 10–20s with a retry-after header. Pros: preserves model quality. Cons: greater client-side complexity.
- Suggest we propose both in the SLA: automatic model-size fallback with a configurable threshold + optional client queuing fallback.

I’ll prep a short appendix for the SLA doc describing expected cost delta and quality tradeoffs.
